title: [Feature] allow searching commit changes: git log -S -p
summary: GitToolBox is a great addition to native intellij git support. One highly demanded feature (205 votes) that has not been prioritized by jetbrain, is ability to find git commits from keyword within changes https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log/2.19.0#Documentation/git-log.txt--Sstring > -S > Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified string (i.e. addition/deletion) in a file. Intended for the scripter’s use. > See related jetbrain feature requests: * https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IJPL-84839/Wanted-Same-functionality-as-git-log-S-git-log-G-available-in-Find-Commit * https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/IJPL-172419/Allow-search-for-a-specific-string-within-the-actual-changes-made-in-commits-git-log-S-support I'm currently using the following workaround workflow to search commits whose content diff contain "someonelesechange" * git log -S "someonelesechange" -p --all --author=... > someonelesechange.log * open someonelesechange.log in the editor * search for keyword "someonelesechange". "next occurence", "previous occurence" Limitations of this workaround: * tedious to go to next commit * tedious to do additional filter out (e.g. author, path) * log file can be large and consuming lots of memory Would GitToolbot be able to add this feature to the native git log view, * with a new "search commit content" text box * then only displaying matching commits, * and enhancing the git log view with a "next occurence"/"previous occurence" of the search keyword, that would move focus in the diff on the matching occurence, among with highlighting match ? Having support for regexp would a nice second time improvement https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log/2.19.0#Documentation/git-log.txt--Gregex > -G > Look for differences whose patch text contains added/removed lines that match .
